utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Despodov.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I continue with my questions, I would kindly ask for the assistance of the usher. Can we give the witness a binder, yet again?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, you remember that yesterday, in response to the question put by my learned friend, about the NLA?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Inter alia, you mentioned Muratovo Djade. Do you remember that? ?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is, in actual fact, a road that links through Skopska Crna Gora, the area of Kumanovo, going above the village of Ljuboten, and it links this area to the border with Kosovo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As for the defence of the City of Skopje and an effective struggle against terrorist attacks, this area was of exceptional importance; can you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was of special importance also due to the fact that, at that time, in the area of Southern Serbia, Presheva, and Podujevo, as well, bordering with the area of Kumanovo, there were also terrorist attacks taking place, terrorist attacks launched by Albanian terrorist groups?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this way, if you agree with me, the link between the terrorist groups from Southern Serbia through the area of Kumanovo, and via Muratovo Djade, a road you referred to, became direct to the area bordering with Kosovo, and it was in Kosovo that these groups had their logistic support?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that period of time, when, together with your battalion, you were deployed on the slopes of Skopska Crna Gora, is it correct that terrorist attacks were not only directed against police and military facilities but also civilians? Journalists were attacked, workers, and then the water supplies of cities were cut off, all of this with a view to intimidating the Macedonian population and expelling them from the area where they had always lived; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these were some of the reasons due to which, in June 2001, a command for the defence of the town was established, consisting of 1st Guardist Brigade, inter alia?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at a document, which is in tab 8 in your binder. The number is 1D-331.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Macedonian version starts with 1D-3042, and the English version with 1D-3048. In the upper left-hand corner, you can see the letterhead of the Command for the Defence of the city of Skopje, and we are going to wait for the document to appear on our screens. 1D-331 is the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Which tab is it, please, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, Mr. Despodov, in the upper left-hand corner, it says: "City of Skopje Defence Command." The date is the 11th of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask for the last page of this document to be displayed briefly. The Macedonian number is 1D-3047, and the English is 1D-3053. On this last page that you see, that is, page 6 in the Macedonian language, if you can see it in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the right hand lower corner there is the signature of the commander, Major-General Sokol Mitrovksi; is that correct? Is it correct that the commander, Major-General Sokol Mitrevski, was appointed head of the defence of the town of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sokol Mitrovski, not Mitrevski. Yes, he was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could we go to the first page, yet again, and can we look at paragraph 1, please. It says in paragraph 1: "As a consequence of the establishment of and actions by the armed formations of Albanian minorities in the territory of Kosovo, and the choice of armed violence as a method for resolving possible dissatisfactions in political demands, diversion terrorist groups of the Albanian minority, with mis-composition, both by motives as well as origin, are active for a longer period of time on the Territory of the Republic of Macedonia. Their strength is variable. "After encountered failures in the clashes of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia in the populated places on the Eastern slopes of Skopska Crna Gora, noticeable are the efforts by the terrorists to transfer the actions to the region of Skopje and to facilities of vital importance for the normal life of the population and for the operation of bodies of state authority. The terrorists control of village of Aracinovo, where they set up barricades on the roads and conduct preparations for the defence of the village. Evident are their incursions also in neighbouring villages." My question, Mr. Despodov, is whether this is an accurate description of the situation that you testified about and that actually led to the establishment of the command for the defence of the town of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 1, in the last paragraph in the Macedonian version - so it is paragraph two, subparagraph (2) - there is a task that is established. Through this order, what is determined is coordinated action with organs of the Ministry of the Interior. Can you see that as well?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This task is in line with your own understanding of the powers that the Army of the Republic of Macedonia has in relation to the police forces in carrying out combat actions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at paragraph 3. 1D-3044 is the Macedonian version, and the English version is 1D-3050. In the middle of this page, you see paragraph 5(3)?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It says here that it is the task of the 1st Guardist Brigade without 1 Infantry Battalion. Can we agree that this task pertains to the brigade that your battalion belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In subparagraph (2), the task is established. It says here: "By supporting upon favourable ground facilities and in joint action with the 16th Brigade and the 1st Guardist Brigade and the forces of the Ministry of the Interior that are active within or in the direct vicinity," and so on and so forth, a specific task is being established. Can you agree with me, Mr. Despodov, that this task, established by the order of the City Command, determines the tasks that are to be carried out by the Ministry of the Interior as well, in line with the authority that the Army of the Republic of Macedonia has in preparing, planning, and carrying out combat actions?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only can we clarify one thing, make it more precise? You have mentioned here the 16th Infantry Brigade and the 1st Guardist Brigade. This is the abbreviation of one GBR, 1st Border Brigade, which was already deployed, and was since then under the command of the command of the defence for the city of Skopje. Also in the command for the defence of the City of Skopje, the commander of which was General Sokol Mitrovksi, there was a permanent representative from the Ministry of the Interior who was responsible for the coordination and planning of the joint operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. And as you said yesterday, at the moment when this coordination is brought to a point when a combat task has to be carried out, then the police units are under the command of the army; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you to look at page 4 of this same document. 1D-3045 is the Macedonian version, and the English version is 1D-3051, and I'm referring to paragraph 8.2. In this paragraph, tasks are established for the intelligence security; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As it says here, the focus of the intelligence security is the timely discovery of diversion terrorist groups and collection of data regarding their deployment, strength, armament, and direction of movement. In subparagraph (3), it says that this information has to be exchanged with the Ministry of the Interior. Is that the task that the units of the army had in defending the city of Skopje and in line with this order?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at the next page, page 5. 1D-3046, and the English is 1D-3051, the last paragraph, and then it continues on page 52. So I am referring to 8.3, which refers to security. I am going to ask you to look at the last subparagraph, that is, number 3, and it says that the commands of units are to get in touch with the police stations in their zones of responsibility and conduct mutual coordination of activities. What is referred to here is what you mentioned a few moments ago, that that is that every unit command has to ensure that there is presence of a representative of the Ministry of the Interior for coordinating, planning, and carrying out activities within their own zone of responsibility. My question: Is that the task that you tried to explain when answering my learned friend's questions, when you said that your battalion established and maintained cooperation with the police station of Mirkovci and the police station of Cair?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edina, if I may provide a more detailed explanation here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also had the duty to establish contact with one station for counter-electronic fight, so-called, which was located at Ramno, and the task of which was to provide surveillance of all telephone conversations between us, between the terrorists. All participants in the telephone and radio communications and any data received in the scope in which they were needed for my command were communicated to me. We would exchange them orally. Also, I had a contact with - I may feel free to say - with a patrol that was a secret, undercover patrol. I was the only one who knew about them, and they knew about me, while my commander did not know about me. I was not permitted to tell him, actually, adhering to the provisions of this order. Also, the army, the intelligence sector, had also a movable intelligence patrol, undercover, which was active in the areas of Strima and Matejce, the area where the terrorist movements were observed. So I would communicate all this communication necessary scope, verbally, to my command. While part of my command, I would communicate directly to the sector, to the officer in charge of the security and intelligence in the commander for the defence of city of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So if we look at the order itself, and having heard what you said in addition to that, there was a single plan for the defence of the city, within which you carried out certain tasks; namely, both army units and the police, as ordered by that plan; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in view of the fact that the witness answered the questions that he is familiar with from the order, I would like to move that this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D-81, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, now I'd like to ask you to look at the document under tab 9, and 672 is its 65 ter number. The Macedonian version is on page N000-699, whereas, the English version is N000-6993-ET. Yet again, this is a document of the Command for the Defence of the City of Skopje, dated the 14th of June, 2001. If you look at page 3, that is to say, the last page of this document, N000-6993, Macedonian, and N000-ET, in the English version, yet again, you see that this order was issued by Major-General Sokol Mitrovski; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 1, N000-6991, and the English is the same number, but it only has an "ET" at the end. Please look at paragraph 5, which establishes tasks of units. In subparagraph 5.1, it is established that the 1st Guardist Brigade is to march in the following direction, barracks of Elendin, village of Ljubanci, and Elendin barracks, village of Orman, and to take up a defence zone according to Defence orders. Tell me, is it correct that this is your Guardist Brigade and that the area of deployment towards the village of Ljubanci actually pertains to your battalion?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask that this document be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D-82, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you explained yesterday, Mr. Despodov, to my learned friend, your battalion was deployed in the area including Ljubanci, Ljuboten, Brodec, and Rastak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is actually the area of the slopes of Skopska Crna Gora that was of exceptional strategic importance for the defence for the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Practically, it is that area which you described a few moments ago as the area of communication among terrorist groups and their links from Kumanovo to the border of Kosovo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is the area that provided logistic support to the terrorist groups, both from the area of Skopje and the area of Kosovo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While responding to my learned friend's questions and in accordance with the order that you received, your task was, first of all, to have the battalion deployed in the area and to prevent attacks, incursions, and all other intentions to be carried out by the terrorists vis-a-vis the city of Skopje; generally speaking, was that the mission of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The order of General Sokol Mitrovski is practically a decision reached at operational level. These tasks that were derived from that, as far as you're concerned, were a realisation of this order at tactical level; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, you were not in the area before, and you did not know the area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was the reason for the first thing that you do in accordance with the order provided, to conduct a reconnaissance of the area and to define the strategic items or points for the deployment of your battalion so that you can complete the task that was provided to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A little while ago, you already said that you established communication with certain police intelligence and other units. Is it correct that also you established cooperation with the authorities in the Municipality of Cair and the Village of Ljubanci so that you will have full information regarding the situation in that particular area?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with one addition, if possible, Mrs. Edina. Also with the local authority, that is to say, the community unit in the Village of Ljubanci, I also established a contact -- INTERPRETER: Interpreter's correction: Ljuboten. Established a contact with the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify this. So, as a battalion command, you have had meetings with the appropriate authorities in the Village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You explained the task that the army had at this area, and also you told them that you expect support from the citizens in order to implement the mission; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I already mentioned in my previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Probably, you also told them that the army is going to undertake measures in the event if sabotage and terrorist groups appear in this particular area?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you maybe remember, the responsible person for the village of Ljuboten was Kenan Salievski, and for Ljubanci, Atanas Kostencovski. Were these the people that you had established contact with?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village of Ljuboten, besides Kenan, there were two more representatives. One, the teacher, his name is Djeljo, and I have known him for some time. Since in the military barracks of Ilinden, the place with the park with the grass, he was the one taking care of the grass for several years. And the other representative, I only know that he was called Zlatar. I don't know his precise name. I can't not recall it. Zlatar, because he had a shop selling gold in the old market in Skopje. However, according to my assessment, the person in charge with Mr. Kenan. I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. Yesterday, you said that a large part, maybe 90 per cent of the composition of the battalion, were reservists; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as far as I can remember, you said that this was a great problem for the battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a problem for me, personally, not for the battalion; for me as a commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I was to understand this correctly, you can tell me if I'm wrong, this meant that every single month you have to conduct new training, and it was very difficult to place under effective control this large number of new people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. However, there were other problems much more complex than this: Fighting against alcohol, lack of discipline, voluntary actions. The people did not have appropriate professional -- or in the army, we call these military record specialty; that is to say, to be engaged in my battalion at the position that he was trained for or the training that he completed when he was serving his regular army duties. In order to clarify this, I will provide you with a practical example for a single person; a military reservist. He was in the army, for instance. He was an assistant for the transport complex, 9A15, and he was just an infantry soldier or a cook in my own battalion. So this way you can get a good idea what was the problem. This person did not know how to even hold his weapon, and he was looking at his rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So we can agree, after everything that you said, that you had serious problems in placing under effective command a large part of your battalion the whole time while you were there at this particular location?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I say that you also had additional problems, and these were problems related to the collection of relevant information with respect to the presence and influence of the NLA in the region in which you were deployed?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, like you mentioned earlier, you had a meeting with representatives from the village of Ljuboten, and at the beginning, you believed that some major problems cannot originate from this village; however, soon afterwards, you started receiving information which was extremely important for you also with respect to the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The information that you received from your subordinates, but also from other sources that you described, were talking about major movement in the village of Ljuboten, especially during nighttime; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your soldiers did not dispose of technical means so that to be able to monitor all the movement that was going on in the village throughout the night?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, certain information was pointing out the fact that it was a transfer of logistic support for the activities of the NLA in some other regions; was this the information that you had?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier - I don't know, maybe I have mistaken whether you have said it before the Court or in your statement - but you noticed that the farmers from Ljuboten would go to the mountains with a large number of sheep, and they would come back with a reduced number of sheep; is this the information that you had?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And if you allow me, if Your Honours allow me, I would like to give a more detailed description so that you can get the whole picture, what was going on. On Skopska Crna Gora, with the exception of Ljubotenski Bacila, where the region of this shepherd's cottage belonged to the area of the village of Ljuboten, there were some other cottages, as well. One of them belongs to the family of Kekenovski; also in the area of Ljubanci village. In the area of the village of Rastak, there were also Rastanski Bacila, then in the other village at Bulacani Cresevo, from Ljubotenski and Ljuboten to the right side to Aracinovo. Every single village had its own location for sheep-herding in the mountains. Since July, as you already explained, the Albanian terrorists visited all these, let's say, Macedonian locations, and they were threatening the farmers they should go down because this is Albanian territory, otherwise they would be killed. So the only place remained was the Ljubotenski Bacila. Before I came with my battalion up there, I asked this question: How is it possible to resolve this problem? Because, obviously, I will have a problem. The farmers -- the villagers would like to go to the shepherds' cottages, to give them food, to take cheese, et cetera, but I knew what was the tension between the reservists, and there might be some negative consequences. And in the conversation with Mr. Kenan and other representatives from the local authorities, this is a problem that I have mentioned to them. However, they guaranteed that nothing is going to happen. However, time has shown that what they promised did not happen, actually. On the 10th, the vehicle was mined and ten people died. I apologise. I was trying all the time through the local authorities, through my superiors, for these cottages to be dislocated because of these security reasons, because I was no longer able to guarantee that none of my soldiers is going to undertake anything on their own, because I took all the measures that was possible, because there were reservists who were shooting the sheep, the cows, and I undertook certain measures that were under my competence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am quite sure that you, Ms. Despodov, undertook all the measures necessary. However, I am interested in the intelligence data which, besides the fact that shepherds were going there and some of the sheep would remain there, did your soldiers also in this particular area were able to notice that these shepherds are coming close to the military positions of your battalion and that basically you came to the conclusion that these are not shepherds but people who are trying to collect information about the deployment of the military forces?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was something that was going on, on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also receive information from your soldiers that from time to time they would find pieces of uniforms or ammunition that would be a proof of sporadic fighting in certain areas and other evidence that convinced you about the presence of NLA in this region and their direct connection or link with the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the deployment and the position of the companies and parts of companies, as you pointed it out, that my learned colleague has shown during your testimony, is it correct that you could notice the citizens of the village of Ljuboten practically lives in the traditional manner in houses that are surrounded by tall walls, which practically made it impossible to observe the events and what is going on in the village itself from your positions?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to put it to you that practically these walls were a true fortification of every single house, would this merely represent your own opinion about the organisation of everyday life in this village?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Edina, I am going to answer this question with a professional term. There was no need for additional fortification setup of these positions or houses. They were protected in such manner that you would need much more explosives in order to bring it down or to tear it apart.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now I would like to ask you a few questions regarding the event that happened on the 10th of August, 2001, and that is the mine that was placed in the area of Ljuboten Bacila. You were discussing this event with my learned colleague. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, you were not present at the command post on the 8th and 9th. These were your holidays; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, practically, on the 10th, in the morning, you came to your position?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Around 8.30, while you were talking to the company commander, Mario Jurisic, you heard the explosion?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment, it seemed to you the explosion came from that particular area where this company commander was located at?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a commander, you immediately asked for additional information?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that very fast your commander, Mario Jurisic, informed you that a truck with reservists who were coming back from their shift passed over a mine and probably there are serious consequences?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You immediately issued the order for certain measures to be undertaken to find out what are the consequences and to help out the people who were part of this incident?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, Mr. Despodov, is it correct that, besides this response by the commander to gather information and to help out his soldiers, you were also very angry because the transport of soldiers with trucks to the position was contrary to your order?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, your order was for the soldiers to be transported only to a certain area by trucks and then they should continue on foot because you were aware about the presence of NLA in that area and the possibility for mines to be placed on this road that was used by the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, basically, you came to the conclusions that one reservist alone, contrary to your order, made this decision that a truck should be used for the transport to this particular location where the shift was supposed to be changed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And regarding what you were saying related to the problems with the reservists, this is one more obvious example that the reservists were not under a full effective control by you, as a commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You already testified about this before the Court. Other evidence has been provided in this respect. And you found out that seven soldiers lost their lives on the spot, that eight of them have been injured, and one of those eight later on died from the injuries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Upon your order, the company commander immediately went to the position where the mine incident occurred, but the injured soldiers there and your soldiers who went there to assist them were exposed to an intensive attack by the terrorist groups which planted the mine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The fire exchange lasted for several hours?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around three to four hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of the difficult access to assist the injured, you asked for the assistance from a helicopter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the whole operation of assistance to the injured soldiers, your orders were such that people should shoot towards the terrorists and not toward the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If that particular day any type of grenade or other damage should have been caused to the village of Ljuboten, would it be possible to say that this was lack of precision in the firing from the position of the NLA or improper behaviour from one of the reservists in your battalion?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whether both or -- is it possible that both things have happened? Was it possible for a grenade to meet, that the NLA was shooting at a position above your village; is this possible?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer not by "yes" or "no," I will say 99 per cent, according to my information and my recollection, is that such a grenade can -- could have been fired only by the terrorists, but 1 per cent I still leave enough room and chance that such an action could have been undertaken by one of my reservists. However, I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Amongst the casualties, there were two soldiers from the neighbouring village of -- Macedonian village of Ljubanci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague yesterday has shown to you the report that you have submitted pertaining to this incident, and I would kindly ask you to look at this report that can be found under tab 12. This P301, and it was 65F248.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, can you show this to me, because we did not arrange all the evidence, the exhibits that have been tendered yesterday. Yes, precisely, this is the report I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And yesterday you recognised this report as one of your own; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, before that you reported verbally to your superior command about what had happened; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 of this document, there is something that you were asked about. You were asked about a part of a particular sentence, the last sentence, rather, in which there is a reference to cooperation with members of the Ministry of the Interior who arrived in the afternoon hours, and you explained that this was a regular police patrol that soon left the site. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, this is a police patrol of the Mirkovci police station; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you to look at the document which is at tab 14. Its 65 ter number is 236. There is just one English page and one Macedonian page. This is a report of Brigade General Zvonko Trencovski to the Office of the Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Macedonia of, and information is provided herein about the medical evacuation that took place by helicopter; namely, the evacuation of five wounded members of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia from a position between Ljubanci and Ljuboten. What I'm asking you now is whether this information, to the best of your recollection, pertains to the engagement of helicopters for medical evacuation. Is that what you had asked for on the 10th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document also be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it already an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The previous one was, the report on the 10th, so the one that was in tab 12, that is now Exhibit P301. Now I would like document 14, the document that is in tab 14 that refers to the use of a helicopter, and it bears the 65 ter number 236, I would like that document to be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We didn't pick up on the transcript the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D-83, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your subordinated officers informed you that in this exchange of gunfire with the terrorists, who had planted a booby-trap, several terrorists were killed; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also received information that three or four armed persons entered the village; is that the information that you received on that day from your units?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Despodov, that from the positions where the police was, that is to say, the police of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia, it was possible to notice that these armed persons were entering the village and that they had identical information?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I was not able to follow you precisely. Would you be kind to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Perhaps the question was a bit imprecise. You stated that you had received the information from your units, that three or four armed people entered the village of Ljuboten. I'm interested in learning whether the police forces from the positions that you marked yesterday, when asked by my learned colleague, from Straista, let's take that example, were they able to see the same, that those armed people were entering the village?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to police officers that were stationed at the check-point in the village of Ljubanci, I don't think they would have seen that. I don't believe it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, if the police were also to report on the same things taking place, that would have meant that they had received information from their own people, their own patrols on the ground, or that they received that information from you, through your exchanges of information; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I'm going to ask you to look at the document that is under tab 15. The 65 ter number is 302. As you can see from what it says in the upper left-hand corner, it is a telegram from the police station at Mirkovci, and it is signed by the commander of the police station, Slavko Ivanovski. This is a person that you cooperated with; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this telegram, it says that on the 10th of August, at around 1530 hours, by the patrol of the police station Mirkovci, which was set up above the village of Ljuboten, i.e., operation officer Dusan Todorov informed that in the village of Ljuboten, along the stretch from the school towards the cemetery, on the left side of the road in the houses of the families Angelovksi, they noticed three persons in black uniforms and armed with automatic weapons. That is actually the same information that you got from your soldiers on the ground; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Your Honours, could this document please be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D-84, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, yesterday, did you -- or rather, at the time, did you have knowledge to the effect that some citizens of Ljuboten had joined the NLA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to my learned friend's question, you mentioned that you already had knowledge about Xhavid Asani; do you remember having mentioned that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask the Registry to help me, if possible, in terms of showing document 670. That is its 65 ter number. That is part of the diary of the 1st Guardist Brigade. The Prosecutor tried to show it to the witness yesterday, and due to the translation it was withdrawn. Now I would just like to have N001-1428 displayed - that's the English text - and page N001-4725 - that's the Macedonian version. And if possible -- I'm sorry, maybe I misspoke, maybe I did not give the right number for the English text. Oh, I see. Actually, it is correct for the English version. For Macedonian, it should be -- oh, it is correct. And if possible, before this big middle line, can we show the last part that says: "On the 11th of August, at 1520 hours"? Could it please be enlarged a bit?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, can you see this information that is recorded here in the brigade logbook on the 11th of August at 1520 hours? In the next column, we see the source of information; that is, the command of the defence of Skopje. The content of the information is that Gezim Ostreni ordered Xhavid Asani to carry out an attack at Rastak and Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then in the next column, who is supposed to be informed? In the next column, it says, first, the commander of the 1st Guardist Brigade, then the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Guardist Brigade, and down here it says Captain Pavlov. Is this the information that you were aware of, Mr. Despodov?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And I was given the task to act accordingly, corresponding to this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask that this document, part of the diary of the 1st Guardist Brigade, be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise. Just for clarification, the issue that the Prosecution have with respect to this particular this document, are that the translation in English was actually received in the Macedonian Government; and in reviewing each entry, it appears that on this particular page, N001-4728 of the English version, there are at least two entries missing that have not been translated. So our office actually had asked CLSS to translate them, the entire log, into English, which we have received. And my information was that yesterday it was requested that the full and complete English translation be uploaded into e-court; however, I see that probably hasn't happened not taken affect yet. I just wanted to note for the record that there are some are entries missing, with respect to this particular page on the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because of that, would it not be preferable to await the full translated version, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we certainly do not mind waiting. Now it can just be marked for identification and then the entire document can be admitted into evidence subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will mark the document for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D-85, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Despodov, tell me, this great misfortune, when eight young people lost their lives, did that cause unrest among the population in the area of your battalion, especially the population of the village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: A great deal of unrest.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that already on that day, several hundred people from Ljubanci arrived before your command, asking you for weapons so that they could go and look for terrorists and protect themselves from future attacks?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you and later your brigade commander personally, when he came as well, made a major effort in order to calm down, at least in part, the population that was so agitated?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information or do you know that these persons, the local population, asked the police station in Cair also, not only you, for weapons?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether they were looking for weapons at the police station Cair, I don't remember that anyone informed me about this. I only know about my situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also don't believe, probably, or maybe you do know - well, tell us if you do know - whether part of these people on Sunday had entered Ljuboten, actually.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you do not preclude that possibility, you do not rule it out?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask the witness to wait before starting answering.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On Saturday, the 11th of August, you were carrying out preparations for the funeral of the young men in Ljubanci; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I've spent almost the entire day in that, more than half of the day, dealing with that duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Doing this kind of work, you could observe that people were still highly agitated?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: To say sincerely, if it weren't for the people from the village who, as military reservists, served in my unit, without their assistance, maybe I wouldn't have been here today.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this unrest or, how shall I put this, this fury on the part of the people was manifested after the funeral that had been attended by several thousand people?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the funeral itself, could you notice that it wasn't only the locals from Ljubanci who were present, but that people had come from the broader area, from Skopje and from other areas around Skopje; could you observe that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to go back to a part of your testimony that pertains to the arrival of the representatives of the police on Friday, the 10th of August, their arrival in your command at the elementary school. As you said in your testimony on Friday, Slavko came to your command, and that would be Slavko Ivanovski, commander of the Ljubanci police station; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said "Ljube," and that would be Ljube Krstevski, and that would be the head of the Ministry of the Interior in Cair; is that right? ?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then Johan?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And a person who introduced himself as being from the Ministry of the Interior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I can infer this correctly, at the moment when they arrived, you just knew the first two people, Ivanovski and Krstevski; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You first saw Johan then, and he introduced himself as the bodyguard to the President of the Republic; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the other person said what his name was, but that you do not remember the name, and that he was from the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As for this fact, that this person stated to you, you didn't really check it out in any way, did you, in any way?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The fact that they were with persons you knew did not lead to any suspicion on your part as to whether this was a person who just introduced himself as being from the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had no suspicion, I had no reason to distrust what he was saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, to this day, you cannot say with any certainty whether this person did, in actual fact, come from any organ of the Ministry of the Interior; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Speaking about this first meeting on Friday, the 10th of August, if I understood you correctly, you said that Mr. Johan Tarculovski was talking on the telephone and was a bit nervous; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, if I understood you correctly and in accordance with the conversation that was taking place, he gave you the receiver and said, "Is it Mr. Boris Trajkovski, the President of the Republic of Macedonia, who is on the phone"?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You answered the phone, and, undoubtedly, you recognised the voice of President Trajkovski; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am one million per cent certain that it was the President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you explained why you were one million per cent sure, because often you had occasion to meet him or hear the President speaking to the army or somebody else; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When answering some of the questions put by my learned friend yesterday, you said, yesterday, that you believed that this action was legally planned, and you stated that on page 39 of the LiveNote. In actual fact, you proceeded from the fact that the President of the Republic of Macedonia, who is your commander-in-chief, spoke about that action very openly; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was quite clear to you from that that the President of the Republic knew about that action?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that this is a legally-planned action or a legal action, could you agree with me if I say that you reached that conclusion -- actually, if I understand things correctly, that you reached that conclusion because previously you had already had knowledge about the presence of terrorists in the village and that it was only natural to search the village and arrest these terrorists. That is one of the reasons why you would consider this action to be a legal one; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, for you, the legitimacy of this action could be derived from the fact that the President of the Republic, as the Commander-in-Chief, was at least informed about this action?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the conversation that you had and the President's question as to whether you had received an order, you could conclude that it would have been quite legitimate, in terms of the President's authority, that he was the person who had ordered the action because he did have the authority to order the use of police forces; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mrs. Edina. And, Your Honours, if you allow me, I would present a little bit of further clarification. My hesitation whether to accept the cooperation and the proposal from the Ministry of the Interior representative was, in actuality, lack of order that would regulate this, regulate who would be the responsible leader of the action, who would be the commander. If I had an order stating Despodov is the person responsible for the action or the representative of the Ministry of the Interior is responsible for the action, then I would have accepted the cooperation with the police without any further discussions. But I did not want to place myself or them in a situation where, if something happened after the action, if there was abuse of -- misuse of force or something, then somebody would need to be responsible for this. And so in that sense and with that purpose, I requested to see the order, who would be responsible. If something goes wrong, who would then be responsible? Had I had such order, it is irrelevant whether in writing or verbal. So this is the way I understood the President, that he would say with the General Sokol how things stand and he would come back to me and informed me. Why I never received any further information, I'm not very clear to this very day, and this is why things are as they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understood completely your position and I understood your testimony; but considering that you stated that it was a legitimate action, my question was just to clarify this. Does it mean that the legitimate organ ordered it, the President, for instance, and that the target, the village, was legitimate because there were terrorists there who needed to be arrested; is that the basis for you to say that you considered this action to be legitimately planned, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, perhaps it would be time to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, my learned friend, the Prosecutor, showed you yesterday the reports composed by Ljupco Kostadinov, security officer in your brigade, and the colonel, Blazo Kopacev, commander of your brigade. Do you remember these documents being shown to you?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will not show you those documents again. I would only like to ask you: Do you remember that at the very beginning of the report by Mr. Kostadinov, it states that some people arrived to the house of Johan Tarculovski in Ljubanci and the distribution of some weapons was discussed there; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning your answers given to my learned colleague, I would like to ask you: Is it true, actually, that you did not go to the house of Johan Tarculovski during those days and you could not know what took place in that house?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the present day, Mrs. Edina, I do not know which house belonged to Mr. Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So then I could understand that you never went to the house of Johan Tarculovski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, to this date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you personally did not see, neither on the 10th nor on the 11th, any distribution of weapons, if it took place at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you could not testify that there was a truck in Ljubanci, a truck from the Ministry of the Interior, because you never saw that truck personally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen it in Ljubanci. My trucks, army trucks, were there. Some are similar in colour, in appearance. The difference is only in the license plates. If somebody misunderstood an army truck to be a police truck, I could not make a comment on this. I have not seen a police truck there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that you spent half of the 11th of August in the preparations for the funeral?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than half a day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, possibly, during that time in your command, other people arrived for the preparations for the funeral; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, people came from everywhere, from the Ministry, from other bodies, from other villages, from the city, from everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But is it correct that no Jeep Cherokee came to your command or was stationed there. There was no Jeep that could be seen in the yard of your command? Have you seen any such Jeep?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen such Jeep. It was only before. I apologise. Mr. Kenan came once or twice with his Jeep, but I do not remember the make. It was a large Jeep, something similar to the Grand Cherokee. But it was earlier, not during those days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you agree with me, Mr. Despodov, considering that you had communication with the police, that the police in the area of Cair, the police that you encountered, did not have an armoured vehicle, BTR?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police had only Hermelins, and BTR is an armoured battle vehicle that is usually possessed by the army. And the army did have one, but it was up there at Malo Ramno, Ramno, Tanusevci, and Brest. While in the area of the villages Pobozje, Ljubanci, Ljuboten, Rastak. And to the right hand side towards the other villages, there was no such vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Hermelin that the police had, that Hermelin did not have weapons mounted on it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a vehicle used only to transport the police patrols that were patrolling those areas or were patrolling the spaces between my companies. It was their duty to do it. They would drive down the asphalt road, then walk on foot, complete their duties, and come back. But I'm now speaking again about the area Pobozje, Brodec, Ramno, and upwards towards Tanusevci, where there is asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you also explained that the command of your 2nd Company was located in the children's holiday resort not far from the St. Ilija monastery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you could arrive to this command, to this holiday resort by cobblestone; that's the road that leads to that holiday resort?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially cobblestone, partially asphalt which is already dilapidated. It is predominantly cobblestone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And anyone who would go to the command of your 2nd Company would be seen by the members of that company or other members of your battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And some persons who were coming unannounced or who shouldn't be there would be -- you would be informed about their presence there?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And if you allow me, I would elaborate this in greater detail. Within that deployment of that company, as I mentioned before, there was a free area that I could not cover with -- I could not cover with people, and it was very important because the wells for the so-called -- wells that supplied water to the village of Ljubanci were located there. So there was a police patrol that secured those wells, and its composition was different. It sometimes was two officers' strong, sometimes five, depending on the needs, and I would not go into this. And these patrols did not have any special authorisation from me to go there. They just had a general authorisation, and they would just declare their presence at the ramp where they needed to pass. They would say, "We are the patrol," and those people would then inform the patrol commander, and he had the general authority to approve their entry so that they could complete their task. Sometimes they would stay there longer, sometimes shorter. Sometimes they would stay there overnight, depending on the task they had, the task given to them by their commander. I did not need to be informed about it or have any more detailed information about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But at any rate, on the 10th, the 11th, or 12th, you never received any information that somebody, some vehicle with journalist markings, especially markings of foreign journalists, had approached that area where your 2nd Company was stationed or actually never came to the vicinity of the monastery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that it was possible that anyone came there by a car without having been observed. I think there's no way that this could have happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering the questions of my learned friend, you testified yesterday that on the Sunday morning you received from the subordinate officers from the ground, you received information that they were under an attack from the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also shown two reports from your subordinate officers, Nikolce Grozdanovksi and Mario Jurisic; do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you testified earlier, Mario Jurisic was a commander of the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Nikolce Grozdanovksi was the commander of the Mortar Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you now, Mr. Despodov, this question might be a general one, before I continue with the line of questions related to this event, considering -- I apologise to you. You are a major. Your rank is major.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I am a civil servant. While at that time, in 2001, I was a major; and in 2003, in December, with a delay of two years, I was promoted into lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Lieutenant-Colonel. I read this in your previous statement. But at any rate, as a person with military education and such high rank, you would know that the superior officer is always basing their decision on the information received from the subordinate officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, practically, without that confidence, relying upon the information that you receive from the subordinate officers, such line of command could not be working, a line of command as the one established within the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when you received the information from your subordinate officers that their positions were attacked, you then absolutely believed that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And because of this, and also in accordance with your right to respond with fire whenever the security of your unit is threatened, you then issued an order to return fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, if I understood you well, you issued an order to return fire to the first positions from which shooting came.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then to also return the sniper fire that later came from the area not far from the mosque; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when your subordinate officers stated in their report that they returned fire pursuant to your order, this is absolutely corresponding to what you actually did on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In one of the drawings shown to you by my learned friend, the Prosecutor, you saw coloured markings denoting various positions of your battalions, then the positions of the police, and positions of the NLA; do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some of the positions marked with red circles or dots, regarding some of those positions, you explained that those are the positions of your 2nd Company, and then it was five to six soldiers deployed at those positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, depending on the moment. Sometimes it would be up to ten or 12 when we had more strict measures. I'm referring to stricter security measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, if I remember that sketch well - and you probably remember it better - you know where your forces were deployed. One of the positions was the position Smuk; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Position Smok, not Smuk.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that is one of the positions that is the closest to the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And one could say that it is up on the hill, towering over Ljuboten; and from there, you have a good overview of the most part of the village, especially the part around the mosque; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the documents shown to you, but also from your testimony, it could be inferred that you were informed and that after the location of sniper fire was neutralised, a group of people running towards the forest was observed. Do you remember, approximately, such a report sent to you?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in that report that you received from the ground, there was the information that your positions opened fire against those person who were running away and who shot at positions while trying to escape, and that two or three of those people running were killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And these are the information you received about the events taking place between the morning and then around noon in the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told me, just a while ago, that in your battalion there was a huge number of reservists. Is it correct that in the 2nd Company, as well, there was a significant number of reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that company, it was only the company commander and another officer who came from the regular forces. All the other officers were from the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have information that among those reservists, there were some who were from the Ljubanci village?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when we discussed earlier how difficult it was to have effective control over part of those reserve forces, I'm asking you is it correct that you could not preclude the possibility that some of those reservists, without or setting aside your orders, opened fire from infantry weapons against the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that it could have happened with my knowledge or order or with the knowledge or order of the company commanders or any other superior officers, but there is always the possibility that someone takes things in their own hands and then acts upon their own will. It could not be precluded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you never received any information on that or you don't have any knowledge about it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You could not also preclude the possibility that some of those reservists entered the village on that morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say it with 100 per cent certainty. It is possible that someone did enter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you, as a commander, did not receive any information on that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And just a few more answers, Mr. Despodov --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: A few more questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You clarified the position of Mr. Kostadinov in your battalion and his tasks. Tell me, is it correct that after these events there was an inspection performed at Ljubotenski Bacila at the location where the mine was placed?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no official report by the brigade command or the command for the defence of the City of Skopje, no; whereas, whether other institutions, the Ministry of Defence, the army, the General Staff, or any other governmental institutions made reports, I have no information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, as a soldier, know that the security organs have a dual line of command; one, leading to the commander of the unit where the security organ is located in the structure, and the other vertical that is linked to the security organ of the superior command. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look in tab 31 to document 65 ter 233. There is a page in English and a page in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the top left-hand corner, you see the number of military command and the date, 15th of August, 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the bottom right corner, there is assistant of the command for security, Captain First Class Ljupco Kostadinov written. Also, in this left-hand corner, one can see your name. Are you aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as far as I can see, two things are missing from this document. It is driver's license and passport for two persons who are villagers of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it your unit, the one that found all these weapons enumerated from 1 to 19, at the location where the mine was planted at Ljubotenski Bacila, and are you the person who handed this over to the security organ?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: My reconnaissance patrol found this, and I personally handed it over. I controlled it and handed it over to the security organ. Also, it was recorded in a videotape and photographs were taken as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you stated that you also handed --

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I handed over a driver's license, if I remember well, one issued in 1996. And I can't remember the name of the bearer, but I think it was Kadri Arifovski, Alievski, something of the sort. While the passport had been issued, it was an old Yugoslav passport from the former Yugoslavia, red, bearing those insignia and emblems, and there was several prohibitions to enter certain countries, black stamps. The countries involved were, as far as I remember, Switzerland and Germany. It was an older, outdated passport, but it was found at the location where the mine was planted, where the terrorists planted it on the 10th of August. So whether those persons were there on the 10th or later, on the 12th, because I was attacked on the 12th, I could not say with certainty, but they were found in that vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me whether you remember if one of those documents was for a person from Ljuboten.
