utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both documents belonged to people from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I seek to tender this document into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D-86, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Ms. Despodov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Mitre Despodov, my name is Antonio Apostolski, and together with my learned colleague, Jasmina Zivkovic, we represent Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Today, I'm going to ask you questions with respect to events in Ljuboten and Ljubanci in August of 2001. As my colleague, Edina, I would also like to warn you, especially bearing in mind that I am using the Macedonian language and you speak the Macedonian language as well, so that we will be able to ask questions and respond to those questions quite fast. But still I would like to point out that my questions and your answers have to be interpreted in several other languages, so that is why I will be slower asking questions, and you should wait for the interpretation before you provide your answer so that we can continue. You were the commander of the 3rd Guardist Battalion within the 1st Guardist Brigade in 2001; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your deputy was Sasha Isovski?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 3rd Guardist Battalion composed of three infantry companies and one battery; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 1st Company was stationed in Brodec, and the commander of this company was Saltamarski Zoran; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 2nd Company was stationed at the children's holiday resort at the village of Ljubanci. The commander was Mario Jurisic, and his deputy was Darko Brasnarski; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 3rd Company was stationed in Rastak. The commander was Ferdo Pavlov; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The battery commander was Nikolce Grozdanovksi, and it was stationed at the children's holiday resort; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 2nd Infantry -- the 2nd Infantry Company had six observation points or positions, as follows: Smok, Bomba, Mecka, Volk, Oril, and Jastreb; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask the witness to be shown Exhibit P299.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is a photograph that was used yesterday for you to mark the positions of the 2nd Company upon request to my learned friend from the Prosecution. If you remember those positions that you have marked yesterday on this photograph with red colour, can you please tell us what positions are we talking about, if you remember the photograph that you were marking yesterday? Yes. This is the one.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you refer to the positions that I have marked with red? Yes. Those were the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you mark the first red line with number 1, and can you please tell us what position are we referring to? Please mark the left line with number 1, the one that is lower on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean this one? [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Mark it with number 1, and tell us what position this is.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot precisely define the positions, but we had the positions here, [Indicates], Smok, closest to the village, and then up the hill, Bomba, Jastreb, Oril, Mecka, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Is it possible for you to see the location Kuljm on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark the location called Kuljm with number 1?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the highest peak on the mountain to the north of the mosque. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please mark that location with number 1?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you were told from the villagers that on Sunday, August 12th, 2001, three terrorists left the village and they went in the direction of Kuljm. Can you please mark the direction in which they went?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be this kind of direction, this direction leading from the village to Kuljm, and we have this hill. [Indicates]. So here [Marks]. And we can see the road. And afterwards, there is a mountain road going around Kuljm going towards Jacmenista, Bel Kamen, and Muratovo Djade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark with the number 2 this road that you marked right now; and if possible, can you identify the Smok location with number 3?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I would like to tender this photograph as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D-27, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that on August 10th, 2001, when coming back from shift, eight soldiers died and eight of them were wounded. They were members of the 2nd Company of your battalion under the command of Mario Jurisic; is a is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the stakeout was organised by the NLA terrorist group?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the terrorist group, NLA, had organised other similar terrorist ambushes where other Macedonian soldiers died?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct, then, that on August 8th there was a similar ambush in Karpalak?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that following these types of terrorist acts, the members of the NLA would withdraw in the populated settlements with Albanian population in order for them to mix with the civilian population as part of their tactics?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you had certain information that one part of the group that committed the terrorist attack, on the 10th of August, 2001, withdrew to the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: One part, yes, they tried to go to the village. However, as I already mentioned, they tried.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that even before the terrorist attack, there were certain provocations of the army, since there was regular shooting from infantry weapons towards the members of the Macedonian Army under your control -- command?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you get this type of information for all your positions under your command?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the majority of them. There were no information, only from the mortar unit, because it was in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This means that from the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Infantry Company, you did receive this kind of information about provocations?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Constantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So that it wasn't strange for you to hear shooting from infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an everyday event for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Several days before the ambush organised by the NLA, you ordered that the flocks and the shepherds should move; and, previously, to my learned friend you explained why you did that. Is it correct that you received a warning from the Mirkovci police station that they are going to -- they are going to retaliate because of that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was told that I should pay -- we should pay special attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the reason for that was the fact that you interrupted the way for the NLA from the Skopje and the Kumanovo-Lipko area?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just the communication, but also the logistics security. If I hadn't done that, I believe they wouldn't have undertaken such an action. I apologise. I was always asking myself, if they wanted to conduct an action or ambush of this type, why is it that they haven't done so earlier, because we were there from the 12th of June. But when I ended the logistic support, providing of meat, dairy products, et cetera, and the communication with the shepherds and the village itself, if I hadn't done this, then there would not have been a reason for them to undertake what they did. This is my explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated that amongst the casualties, there were also soldiers from the village of Ljubanci, and that you personally were present at the funeral of the soldiers in Ljubanci on the 11th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were there present other members of the Macedonian Army at the funeral who were not members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I apologise. As far as I remember, according to information I had -- I have, there were none.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were there members from the Ministry of Defence present at the funeral?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no. However, I cannot be certain. Officially, nobody announced themselves that members of the Ministry will be present. This was the procedure. I just wanted to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that after the soldiers lost their lives, you ordered to your soldiers that they should raise the combat readiness level?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your headquarter was in the school backyard in the village of Ljubanci. Were there guards in front of the schoolyard? I am talking about Saturday, August 11th.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the access to the schoolyard was not provided to any person, unless the person was actually invited and expected on the 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the exception of the huge unrest, the attempt by the villagers to exercise certain pressure, and the security could not prevent this. Otherwise, they should have used weapons. This was in the afternoon; and when the situation was normal, nobody could have entered the school without my authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If an unknown person was standing nearby to your command to defence, he or she would have been identified by the guards?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Whether the people who have been I.D.'d, whether the guard was obliged to inform you about this?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's comment: Can you please ask the gentleman to switch on the mic? Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [In English] I don't know why it's happened. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it correct that on Saturday, August 11th, your guards did not inform you that in the vicinity of your post there were some -- there was a foreign journalist present?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I never received such an information.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In the village of Ljuboten -- I apologise. In the village of Ljubanci, there was a police check-point by the house of Bratso, the so-called Chinese Wall?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how people call it, but the precise location was across the -- nearby the football playing field.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that right at the football place, the playground, there was a police check-point?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This is a crossroads that goes to the village of Ljuboten and towards the children's holiday resort.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the football playing field is away from the school where your post was, around three to 400 metres?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This means that the football playing ground is not across the school; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show to the witness D296 or 65 ter 00295, page N001-001-7248.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see this sketch in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can enlarge it a little bit, please. Can we go back because we can't see. Can you reduce it a little bit, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you observe on this sketch where the school is indicated, the school where your command post was located? In English, you can read it. It's spelled S-c-h-o-o-l. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: According to you, this sketch showing Ljubanci is not correct with respect to the location of the football field, and the person who drew this sketch made a sketch which does not correspond with the situation on the ground; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean, Mr. Apostolski, where it reads "school."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You can see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. The exchange between witness and counsel is too quick and you are overlapping all the time, so that the interpreters are finding it impossible to follow what each of you is saying and getting it down onto the transcript. You must be slower, and you must have more pause between each speaker. I must leave it to you, Mr. Apostolski, to watch that carefully in your dealing with the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I do apologise, Your Honours. I will try my best, and I will be slower when asking my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Across the school, as it is depicted on the sketch, we can see written, marked in the English language, "football field," so this is the football playground?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I noticed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: According to your statement, this is a sketch which is incorrect, since the football field is located at another position, another place; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This means the person, who drew this sketch, prepared a sketch which does not correspond with the sketch of the village?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you observe on this sketch, in the middle, above the football field, you can see a cross with a circle beneath it?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If this is the location of the command of the 2nd Infantry Company, I'm sure that it won't be correct to say that members of the Ministry of the Interior are located on the positions marked with the lettering "MUP"; you can see three different positions indicated?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This means that this information on this sketch, according to your opinion, is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. This means that this sketch is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated that on Saturday, August 12th, 2001, the positions of your battalion were under attack by terrorist groups of the NLA from several directions. The position of the 2nd Company was under attack, and you were informed about this by Mario Jurisic. The position of the battery was also under attack. Nikolce Grozdanovksi informed you about this. Under attack was also the 3rd Company, which was at the position in Rastak, and you were informed about this by Ferdo Pavlov; is this correct? ?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Throughout this time, you were at the headquarters, command post, at the school, and you told them that they should respond to this attack; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You did not see, but you had information from your subordinates who informed you about this?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you indicate and mark the locations from where people shot at your battalion from the direction of Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001, which you considered as legitimate targets?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But if you allow me, the precise location of the targets and more trustworthy, I believe, it would be if it is pointed out by the people who gave me this information, because I didn't have visual possibility. The map that I had by me was a bit old, and maybe there will be some differences. And that is why I will say that if I try to locate the precise position of these targets, I might be wrong. So maybe it would be better to get this kind of information from those people; that is to say, if you have their statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. As targets, on Sunday there was one target outside of the village of Bel Kamen; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And four targets in the village by the old cemetery?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The northern part of the village?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The mosque?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the new cemetery and the area in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I would like to go back to several questions regarding the meeting in the presence of Johan on Friday and Saturday. Did you receive any kind of order by Mr. Johan during these meetings?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was Johan in a position to issue any kind of order to you?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you hear Johan, during the meeting on Friday, to issue orders to the persons who came to this meeting together with him?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you tell anybody that Johan Tarculovski was the owner of the security agency called Kometa?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I apologise. This information, I heard it later on, but this was just a manipulation. I don't know how to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the period from the 10th to the 14th of August, 2001, did you say to anybody that Johan Tarculovski was the owner of the security agency called Kometa?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Motoike, is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, briefly. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, going back to yesterday, on page 2615 of yesterday's transcript, you spoke of coordinated actions between the army units and units of the Ministry of the Interior in carrying out operations in the areas of Vaksince and Slupcane. In 2001, can I ask you, if a soldier in your battalion had misbehaved, would you have disciplined him?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, in reference to your testimony today, on page 8 of today's transcript, you had indicated that you had a duty to contact one station which was to provide surveillance of telephone conversations. Did this particular station have a name?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the name is Ramno. That is the central station. It is a permanent one. It is active even now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And I take it from your earlier answers that Ramno is a particular area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but also its location is within that settlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what do you mean, "settlement"? Where is it located exactly?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not "settlement," it is the area of Ramno. This is a building built during the former state, Yugoslavia. And the army at the time used it as a point for counter-electronic combat or actually wiretapping, recording of all telephone-radio communications and everything. So in military terminology in our systems, this is a station for counter-electronic combat. It surveils the communications. After the dissolution of the former state, that station was taken over by the Ministry of the Interior, and one part of it was held by the military intelligence. They were working together here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So if I can understand you correctly, in 2001, was this particular location, then -- well, let me ask you this: The surveillance that you're talking about that was conducted at this particular station, was that conducted by the Ministry of the Interior alone?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the competences, their responsibility for this task at this station, belonged to the Ministry of the Interior. While in the actual operation, experts from the Ministry of Defence participated as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So the information that you -- well, the duty that you had to contact this particular station, was that the duty to contact, then, the personnel at the Ministry of the Interior who were located there?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: To exchange information with them, the information I would learn through my organ reconnaissance patrols, scouts, et cetera, I would communicate to them, and the information that they held that was relevant for me they would communicate to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And specifically, then, this was communication with the Ministry of the Interior personnel who was located at that particular station?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You also mentioned, on the same page of today's transcript, that you had contact with a secret undercover patrol. Could you tell me, please, when were these secret undercover patrols deployed?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This patrol is something that I learned about after I and my unit took positions in that region. They, themselves, found me at a location while I was touring the unit at its post in Brodec, and they informed me and gave me guide-lines about the ways in which we would communicate and exchange information.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And at the time, then, when you learned about them, could you tell me how long -- if you know, could you tell me how long were these particular patrols in position?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about them, or actually we met - I don't remember well - but sometime around the second half -- no, after the 15th, the 16th of June. I left the positions up there sometime around 23rd, 24th of August, and I then informed my deputy who replaced me as duty of the commander that he had the obligation to communicate with this patrol. So this cooperation continued later, and I think they remained there all the way until the end of all military operations or the cases in that region, all the way until the complete withdrawal of the army from those positions, which was sometime in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So you can only speak to their position or their deployment as of 2001? Am I understanding you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, Your Honour. Would you be so kind as to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, then, you had no information as to when, in particular, what time period these particular patrols were deployed?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about it, as I stated, somewhere around 15th, 16th of June, and they remained there until the end, until the final withdrawal of the army. When did they start acting there, when they were deployed there, I could not say. It was not the subject of my interest.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. That is what I was trying to clarify. Were these particular patrols operated by the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose it was a person from the Ministry of the Interior or the Centre for Security. I don't know, I don't know the names of their sectors. I know that in the army there is a sector called security and counterintelligence. In the police, it might have a different name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. But to your knowledge, then, these particular patrols were operated by the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You also indicated that not even your commander knew about the contact that you had with these particular patrols. Who, in particular, ordered you not to have -- not to relay information to your commander about the contact with respect to these particular patrols?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: That patrol had three officers. One of them is responsible, the commander of that patrol, and I received that order from him., that apart from me, no one else must know about their deployment there, because the more people that knew about it, the more possibilities there were, the larger probability would be for the patrol to be discovered and then it would not continue performing its role.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You indicated that you received the order from the commander of that particular patrol. Why did you take that order from that particular commander?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, obviously we can't understand one another. This is a normal procedure in our practice in such cases regarding certain issues. There are things done, and only a very small number of people is allowed to know about it. Those were the regulations, the applicable legislation, et cetera. Since they were acting in plain clothes, in uniform, depending on the needs, they would go, and the villages populated by Albanians, where Albanians were the majority of the population, they would also infiltrate the positions of the NLA, the terrorists. And now imagine if everybody knew about their existence, or if more people knew about their existence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. If I understand you correctly, then, some of these patrols were operating in, loosely termed, enemy-occupied areas?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the terrorists, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, maybe we aren't understanding each other. I was asking about the commander of the patrol. You indicate that you took an order. Is that because -- you reference regulations. Is that because of some regulation that told you, you had to take an order from the command of a patrol operated by the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, Your Honour, I hope you'll understand me better. In order to collect information about the enemy, in this case the terrorists, it is a rule, a military rule, that I, as a commander of a battalion, need to establish contact and undertake measures, in all possible ways I need to collect information about the deployment, the strength, the armament, the logistics, et cetera, regarding the enemy. And I then communicate all the information I had collected to my superior command. Also, the necessary portion of it I would communicate to the police or the members of the security forces and also the police. Those units that were deployed there to serve those needs on the part of the police had that obligation and duty towards me. Some of those organs, we call them reconnaissance patrols, or observers, or monitors, were working publicly and some were working undercover. And in this sense and for this purpose, we had the agreement that nobody else needed to know about the patrol, nobody else but me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: But with respect to the conversation that you had with Mr. Tarculovski and the other representatives on Friday, 10 August 2001, that information, though, you did not communicate to your superior command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Going back to these secret undercover patrols, could I ask you, if you know, what types of information -- I know you've said there was reconnaissance. What types of information did they report?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the terrorists were located, how strong they were in number, what armament did they have, the direction of their movements, and detail of such type.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And how were these -- how was the specific information that they were reporting, how was that communicated to you?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Verbally, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Via radio, messenger, how was it done? Or via telephone?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Verbally, through personal contact between me and them. In every village, they had their representative from among the villagers, and that person would come to me to have a cup of coffee at the command post or meet me somewhere, because I was moving, touring the positions, and then he would relate information to me. We need to meet at such-and-such location at such-and-such hour, and so I would go there and we would exchange the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And with respect to -- going back to the station that you referred to, that provided surveillance of telephone conversations, can I ask you, did this particular station have access to signals intelligence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is obvious that my learned colleague now speaks about something and the witness now divulges a certain dose of confidential information in his answers. For the witness to be able to better answer, maybe we should move into a private session, because we are now speaking about services, and the divulging of those information to the general public might not be very appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Looking over what has being mentioned here, I would see nothing that would give rise to any national security issue, Ms. Residovic, so please carry on, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, do you recall the question I asked you? That is -- well, let me just rephrase it. Did you have access to signals intelligence, and by that I mean access to intercepts or radio and telephone traffic with respect to the particular area that your battalion occupied?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally didn't, but the information contained in those issues I received in the scope that was necessary for me. I would receive them from the representatives of that station. And if you wish to learn more data about the station, because of the reasons that Mrs. Edina mentioned now, I think I don't have the authority to speak more about the principles and the manner of its operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I actually had one more question with respect to this particular station, and if you'd feel more comfortable I could ask the Court if it's allowed to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ask the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You referenced some personnel from the Ministry of Defence who were also at this station. I believe you might even have referred to them as experts. Could you tell me, which chain of command did these particular persons respond to?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The representatives from the Ministry of Defence were under the command of the Sector for Security and Counterintelligence within the Ministry of Defence, while the representatives from the police had responsibilities towards the police, the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And with respect to these secret undercover patrols, can you tell me whether or not you know whether any of these persons belonging to these secret undercover patrols went into Ljuboten at any time between 10 August 2001 and 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't confirm this with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On page 18 of today's transcript, you refer to homes in Ljuboten that you indicated in your opinion were fortified by walls. If I could show you again the photo of Ljuboten that was shown to you yesterday, it's now been admitted as P00299. And to assist you, we have the photo again in its larger version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could have the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Of course, this particular photo is a hard copy of the photo we showed you yesterday, but it hasn't been annotated by you, which the annotations are reflected in P00299. If you could take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And perhaps we could display it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, again, Mr. Despodov, this is a photo of the Ljuboten village, looking towards the Skopska Crna Gora mountain range, and the homes in the bottom of the photograph are homes in Ljuboten. I just want to point out to you, see this bigger house in the foreground of the picture on the left?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could maybe move it up a little bit so it's displayed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: The one left of that, actually. It's a bigger one. Yes. Do you see there's no walls around that particular house, is there, Mr. Despodov?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if you move the photo to the right --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, I apologise. This house, I suppose the photograph was taken from this part [Indicates], in the area where it is predominantly populated by Macedonians in that village; that is, 30 per cent of the population in this part. This is where the Albanians live from the creek [Indicates], as the slope falls down to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Maybe we could pull the photograph to the usher's left, and if we could maybe focus in on the area where the mosque is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: There's a mosque with the minarets shooting up towards the top.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: This area, then, would be what you've termed as the ethnic Albanian area; is that right, Mr. Despodov?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You can see there are some homes in this particular village that are not -- do not have any walls in front of them. Do you see that in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So not all the homes in the village of Ljuboten had these walls that you've termed as fortifications; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, obviously, you misunderstood me when I stated this. I said that every Albanian house, or 95 per cent of them, are fenced by walls. That is in the tradition of the Albanians in Macedonia and everywhere. And these walls, I never stated that these are fortified by the walls. But in a case somebody decides to use this house as a base or as a point from which they would fire, there is no need for an additional fortification. In order to enter the yard of that house, you need to go through the main gate; or to jump the wall, you need to bring ladders three or four metres' tall, if you go to the house uninvited or if you go there with a hidden agenda. So in this sense, I stated this. If you misunderstood me, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Your Honours, I have just a few more questions, and I see the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you prefer to finish now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: -- you indicated on page 32 of today's transcript that the person whose name you can't remember, who met with you on Friday, 11 August, represented himself as being from the Ministry of the Interior. Can I ask you, was this person also wearing a police uniform, and I believe you stated a camouflage police uniform, with the insignia stating "Police"?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. It was not on the 11th. It was on the 10th, if you are referring to that person. A police camouflage uniform, this is precisely what I stated, bearing police insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And have you ever, in your military career, spoken with someone who represented themselves as being from the Ministry of the Interior, but in actuality they were not?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You also were shown a sketch that was marked and actually has been admitted as D296.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could pull that up, please. It's 65 ter 00299. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Just one question about this particular sketch, Mr. Despodov.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could see it a little bit bigger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You indicated that the position with respect to the school and the football field in this particular sketch is incorrect. Is the school in Ljubanci, should that be to the left of the football field and not to the right, as it's depicted here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you mean Ljubanci or Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I mean Ljubanci. I apologise if I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You were correct. I was concerned you may not have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, is the school depicted in this particular sketch supposed to be to the left of the football field as you're looking at the diagram?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the expert drawing the sketch drew it well, in my opinion, the football field -- I'm now speaking about the football field for football matches, for serious football. If this crossroad is really drawn well where it says the direction towards the village of Ljuboten, this is where the patrol -- the check-point of the police actually was. And the football field would be to the right of the school, between the school and the police check-point, at the crossroad depicted here towards the village of Ljuboten. If it is that football field, it should be to the right from the school. Since I go to the village of Ljubanci even now today, I still haven't seen that a football field was built across the street from the school. This is a densely populated area with private houses. Thank you for that. And just a couple more questions, Mr. Despodov. On page 59 of today's transcript, you indicated that Mr. Tarculovski was not in a position to issue orders to you in 2001. Can I ask you, in August of 2001, who did you receive your orders from?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regards specifically to the work in the command of my battalion, I would receive them from the colonel, Blazo Kopacev; directly some tasks also from the general, Sokol Mitrevski; and some tasks I received directly from the commander-in-chief, the President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in August of 2001, who did the police receive their orders from?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police, I suppose, operated under the same system. This is what the law provides for, the commander. It depends on which unit, which unit is superior to which. I don't know whether you noticed, in all documents displayed today, order by the President, order by the commander for defence of the city of Skopje, the President communicates directly or orders the head of the General Staff. The Ministry of Defence or the Minister of Defence is excluded from that hierarchy of issuing commands and orders. I suppose that - and I'm certain that it is so in the police as well - that for some things the Minister of the Interior is not involved at all in the subordination of the hierarchy of issuing commands. The units from the Ministry of the Interior that are deployed, that are involved in the combat actions, receive direct orders from the Commander-in-Chief. I, as a battalion commander -- to make the situation clearer for you, Your Honour, I, as a battalion commander, would skip, so to say, the company commander, I would issue orders to the reconnaissance patrols that I had established. I personally had established them so I would issue orders to them and they were responsible for the performance of the task to me personally. The company commander did not even know who will do it, what they will do, or where. He just knew that ten people from their company would be under my command for the duration of that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. So to your knowledge, though, the Ministry of the Interior in 2001 had their own chain of command as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is not what the witness stated. I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, my question was: So to your knowledge, the Ministry of the Interior in 2001 had their own chain of command as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the tasks or issues that I've mentioned regarding giving order or an action, they operated under the same system as us, the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm talking about just generally, not specific tasks or issues, I'm asking you: Did the Ministry of the Interior, to your knowledge, have a chain of command as well that's similar to the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat again, Your Honour. The supreme commander is the commander of the ones and the others, and in that line of command, the Ministry of the Interior can be set aside from the subordination. This is regulated in the law. I believe that Mrs. Edina has confirmed this in her assertions made yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance here in The Hague, and you are of course now free to return to your activities in your home country. Thank you again for coming to The Hague and assisting. We will now adjourn and resume at 10 minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hutsch. Unfortunately, we're not going to be able to be too long with you this afternoon, because we're approaching our break, so we will undoubtedly see you again tomorrow. May I remind you of the affirmation you made, which still applies to your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Before we begin, if I could ask the usher to place the witness's binder of exhibits with him, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, when we stopped last week, we had been discussing the events of Saturday, the 11th of August, 2001, and I'd like to ask you now, please, to turn your mind to the events of Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001. Can you tell us, please, what you did on that Sunday morning?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Sunday morning, I woke up around 5.30 and met with my two interpreters to go to the area of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And about what time did you leave for the area of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left around 6.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And where did you go then? Was there some point where you stopped?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were stopped in Radusana area, at a check-point of the police there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is this the area we referred to last week as Observation Point 1?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what kind of car were you driving that day?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were driving like all the time a white Land Rover jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was that jeep marked in any way?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was marked with the TV letters that was usual for journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you wearing anything special that day, you and your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this moment when we entered, we didn't wear something special, but afterwards we put on our flak jackets and later on in the morning our helmets.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you briefly explain, Mr. Hutsch, how you recorded events and things that you observed? What system, if any, did you use?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was using a notebook or -- yeah, a notebook where I wrote in all the things that I saw in the moment when I took it -- when I saw it. And I had a time so that I watched first my clock, I wrote the time inside, and then I wrote notes that I was seeing in this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you have binoculars with you that day?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Apart from writing things down in a notebook, what other tool or tools did you use to record things that you observed that day?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had always a map with me, so I printed in which things I saw, what happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go a little bit more slowly? You said you had a map with you. What, if anything, did you use to record things on your map?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was using a plastic overlay that was fixed on the map so that, with special pens, so waterproof pens, I could mark what I saw in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And these things that you noted on the map, would you also note them in your notebook?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps, if I can ask you to turn to tab 4 in your binder, which I believe has been marked for identification as Exhibit P292.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's missing in my binder, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is, I think, perhaps because our efficient court officer had to take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It can't be displayed at the moment, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. What I'll do is we have a clean copy, an extra copy with us, and I'll ask the witness perhaps to draw a few things that he drew last week, and then perhaps make some additional points, if that is all right. If the usher could put this on the ELMO, please. When I press the letter "ELMO" on my side of the room here, what I get in my computer is e-court. I wonder if that could be changed. I think we now see the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, just very quickly --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if the projector could be raised as high as possible, please, so we can see more of this. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Last week, Mr. Hutsch, you had marked a hill that we refer to as Hill 631. Can you place the letters "631" along that hillside again, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And you had also marked, with an arrow, the area that you indicated as Ljubanci, an arrow headed down. Could you do that again, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could you put a "1" beneath that arrow, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you put the number "1" beneath that arrow to indicate Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And could we move now the map a bit over toward your right, and further, please, further, please. So we see the minaret of Ljuboten there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you mark an arrow from above that -- above that minaret?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could you place a capital "L" to indicate the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe also on this same photograph you had indicated with a circle around the ridge or the valley where the area of Ljubotenski Bacila would be, if we could see it. Could you draw that circle in again, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, that's an awfully big circle.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And next to that small circle, could you write the number "2" --

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: -- for Ljubotenski Bacila. Now if we could just move the map a bit more now to your left so we can still see the -- no. We need to see the area that you've indicated which indicates Ljubanci. Now we can see that. All right. Can you tell us, please, when you got to this vantage point - we're still talking about now Observation Point 1 - what you began to observe there -- let me start a little bit earlier. Approximately, what time did you come to this vantage point, if you can recall, approximately?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, 7.15, 7.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And tell us, please, what you began to observe on that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We ask that the witness be directed not to refer to the notebook which was just taken out of his bag, unless there is a need for refreshment, in which case the Prosecution may or may not decide to ask him to refer to those.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I did not see the witness take that out of his bag. Witness, I'm going to show you portions later on, but I'd simply like to discuss what you have in your mind right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: First of all, when you got to Observation Point 1, do you recall whether the police officers told you anything?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police officers told us that there have been two mortar shootings in the area of Ljuboten at around 6.00, and I think it was -- I suppose it was 7.10.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And then what do you recall -- what did you observe after that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So my first observation, my first own monitoring, was at 8.00 and I think three minutes, another round of mortar shells have been fired into the east entrance of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you recall who, to your knowledge, was firing these mortar rounds at a bit after 8.00 that morning?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think these mortar rounds were fired from the mortar position or the battery position in the area of the monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And can you recall which force, then, would have been firing those mortar rounds?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I believe, this mortar position was an army position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Macedonian Army?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Macedonian Army position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you see the impacts of these shells?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We could see the impacts of these shells in the eastern entrance area of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you notice anything in particular about the impacts or the explosions of these shells?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I think is that they were using delaying indigners [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Igniters, you mean?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Which is the same as detonator?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the Prosecutor and the witness to pause between their respective and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My apologies to the interpreters, and I should have given that warning to myself and to Mr. Hutsch earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the so-called delayed igniters or detonators, how did they work?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are working in a way that the explosion is going around 15 up to 20 metres over the target. So that means especially if you are -- if you would like to destroy so-called soft targets, you have a bigger circle on the ground to hit them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And then later on, what did you then observe after that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, I observed more, on the left side of the circle that I called Circle 1, like a group formation behind an APC to rush down from Ljubanci behind Hill 631 towards Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go a little bit more slowly, please. You said you saw a group -- a group formation behind an APC coming from Ljubanci. Did you observe this group with your binoculars?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What did you observe about this group?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a group around 80 to 100 policemen behind an APC, what I think it was a Hermelin, and they are going towards Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You say that it was a group of policemen. What made you think that these persons were policemen?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage -- most of them were wearing camouflage uniforms, and you could see also the badge -- the police badge on their arm, on their left arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This Hermelin armoured personnel carrier that you referred to, can you recall if there were any weapons on it?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose there were 7.62-millimetre machine-gun on top of this Hermelin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And were you able to observe this group of policemen completely going from Ljubanci towards -- and entering into Ljuboten or did you have any problems?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had a big problem to observe or to monitor this group, because Hill 631 covered the advance of this group; and so when they -- when they left, for example, the centre part of Ljubanci, I even couldn't see this group anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, do you have a blue marker there with you? Is there a blue marker?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If not, I'm wondering if the usher could kindly help us out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, if you could, please, could you draw a line, indicating with the blue marker, indicating the route you saw this group of policemen take with a Hermelin until you could no longer see?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And for the record, Mr. Hutsch has just drawn a disconnected blue line with an arrow at the end. And perhaps could you, to the left of this disconnected line, could you write the number "3", please, Mr. Hutsch, to the left?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. After you lost sight of this group of police officers who were then -- which you couldn't see because of Hill 631 between you, what else did you observe that morning?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a more -- group in the south of the policemen who surrounded the hill in the south and also went towards Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you say "a group in the south of the policemen who surrounded the hill in the south." Was this group starting out again from the Ljubanci area?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did you know the people in this group were policemen?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms with their police badge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, just for the record, were you able to observe whether this group that was more to the south, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were armed with normal Kalashnikov rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the group that you had discussed earlier that went behind Hill 631, before you lost sight of them, do you know whether they were armed?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were armed as well with Kalashnikov rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall whether the group that was further to the south, was it smaller than the group that you had seen of nearly 100 police officers, or was it the same size, or bigger?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was much more smaller, what I suppose around 25 maximum up to 30 police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And apart from the camouflage uniforms that the smaller group was wearing, with your binoculars were you able to see any other things that this group was wearing?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This group, some or most of these police officers were wearing bulletproof vests in a simple version. They were wearing helmets, some of them quite old helmets, not these modern Kevlar helmets.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall what colour were those vests?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The vests were blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If we go back to the photograph now that we can see on the ELMO, you mentioned that they left from the Ljubanci area. How long were you able to watch this group?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this group, yeah, up to this small bush [Indicates], when they entered in this area, the outskirts of Ljuboten. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At that point, did you lose sight of this small group?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you mark that small circle -- well, let's do this a bit more systematically. If you could move the photograph so that we can see Ljubanci again. No. All right. Could you take your blue pen again and make another line showing where you saw this smaller group of policemen travel?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. On the left side of that blue line and just underneath the blue line, could you write the number "4", please.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is there a road there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just a small track.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So was this smaller group of policemen following that track?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And now we see the circle, the blue circle, towards the right where you lost sight of this group. Could you write the number "5" beneath that circle, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, at this point I would, if it won't confuse the record too much, I would tender this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will -- yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Simply an indication for the Chamber, we won't formally object to the admission of this document and won't formally object to the admission of a number of other documents which the Prosecution may seek to tender through this witness. I would simply wish to point out, however, that this should not be interpreted as an admission or concession on the part of the Defence as to the reliability of truth of any of those documents, and it may be the case that the Defence will make further submissions after the cross-examination of this witness in relation to many of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be received as Exhibit P307, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps for now if that photograph could be folded up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, if you could please turn to tab 11 in the binder that's in front of you, which is 65 ter number 167. It begins with ERN number N003-0004.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could first pull up on e-court. Yes. This is the original German version, and the parties and the Judges should also have the English and Macedonian versions with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But if we could just focus now on the German version, that cover page, Mr. Hutsch, do you recognise what you see on the screen there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what is this?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my notebook for exactly this day, for the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And can we turn, please, to the first page, and there's a note related. It says: "Telephone, N. Beqiri, 0748 hours." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What were you referring to here?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were phoning with Nazim Beqiri who is the spokesperson or who was the spokesperson of the NLA to ask him what was going on in Ljuboten. And Nazim Beqiri pointed out that there were signs for attacks of the police forces, that in Ljuboten there were no member of the NLA, that after he knows Ljube Boskoski should be on the way to Ljuboten, and it is the purpose of the NLA to fight back with, probably, in a proper way without being dangerous for the peace process.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It mentions the name Ali Ahmeti below that. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall at the time what was Mr. Ali Ahmeti's position?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: His position was that he should --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, not his position about the events in Ljuboten. What was his, if I can say this, formal position?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the political leader of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, we need to pause, you and I, between question and response. And what were you told about Ali Ahmeti's position with respect to the events in and around Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ali Ahmeti just did phone calls and personal discussions with members of NATO and European Union to solve the problem in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so you recorded this information in your notebook?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time. Would this be the appropriate moment to stop?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you don't have an urgent need to finish something. MR. SAXON. I wouldn't say it's urgent, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will need then to adjourn for the day, resuming tomorrow at 9:00 in the morning.
